decision.rule: A sound a game's menu module starts through its local-sound import is interface audio in Fn's tone policy whatever channel it names: the local class (dry, no send to the listener's room, no medium or occlusion shaping, head-relative at the listener), the announcer class on the announcer channel, authored stereo and surround on their own unsent path.
unchanged: channel numbers and every channel rule (which voice a sound replaces or evicts, RTCW's and ET's one-shot bookkeeping, Academy's 0.75 level below its ambient channel)
every module ABI and import ordinal
the client games' local sounds (cl_cgame.cpp, the Academy, Elite Force SP, Q3Test and IHV hosts)
the legacy mixer, the retail-exact option, which has no tone classes or room sends
the engines' own menus, which already play on local or menu channels
decision.whyNotChannels: Treating the automatic channel at the listener as local everywhere would also move the client games' own listener sounds (Fn's self class: the listener's sound inside the level); translating Academy's or Holomatch's menu channels to a local channel would change which sound replaces which on the listener's entity, a contract retail pins.
decision.invariant11: Retail pins the channel and the level the module hands over; how the engine presents a menu sound is Fn's, and its tone policy already calls UI audio non-diegetic (AudioTonePolicy.h: "Non-diegetic: UI, feedback, and chat that plays outside the level").
